lead: Lakeland plumbing deals with hard aquifer water, sinkhole-prone ground, storms and 1920s homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Lakeland.
risk: hard water scale, cast-iron drain failures and slab leaks
risk_short: hard water, old drains and slab leaks
why: Dixieland, Lake Morton and Lake Hollingsworth have homes from the 1920s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Newer areas to the north and south were built mostly after 1980 on slabs.
Polk County sits on limestone with sinkholes in places, which can shift buried lines. Hurricanes such as Ian and Milton brought flooding and long outages.
water: Lakeland pumps water from the Floridan Aquifer. It is hard, so scale builds up in water heaters and on fixtures.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Watch for new cracks that could mean a shifting line.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
areas: PipeMend works in Dixieland, Lake Morton, Lake Hollingsworth, Beacon Hill, South Lakeland, North Lakeland and every other Lakeland neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Lakeland Building Inspection Division, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.a: Yes. Lakeland's water comes from the Floridan Aquifer in limestone, so it carries a lot of calcium. Scale builds up in water heaters and on fixtures.
